alias_parser_repair.evidence: Checkpoint A-032-039 node 16 stores "… and C7‑Signal‑0 is an alias for C7‑AliasBase‑0." with U+2011 NON-BREAKING HYPHEN. The identifier class [\w.:-] does not contain U+2011, so the name shattered and the parser returned the SPURIOUS pair ('0', 'C7'). After the repair it returns ('C7-Signal-0', 'C7-AliasBase-0').
alias_parser_repair.flag_scope: Reached only under GRM_ALIAS_FOLD_MERGE; OFF stays byte-identical (off_parity re-run).
alias_parser_repair.why_it_matters: A spurious pair is worse than a missed one: it invents an alias relation for a node that asserts none and then tries to merge it. This is the same glyph-shattering SC1.1/FIX-8 was minted for; the module already depended on normalize_glyphs through identifier_set, the parser simply was not using it.

checkpoint_state_finding.consequence_for_the_prediction: The registered prediction (aliases >= 5/8 exact from a single merged-digest mount) cannot be tested on the d030-d250 rows as they stand: there is no edge for A1 to merge, so the ON and OFF arms are the SAME repository. Only the d005 cell exercises the treatment. This is a finding about the fixture, not a result about A1, and the lead decides what to do with it.
checkpoint_state_finding.finding: The C7 r3 checkpoints no longer contain unmerged alias edges at distance >= 30. The ordinary librarian has ALREADY folded the Signal edge and the Jasper base into separate ACTIVE digests (node 16 states the relation; nodes 27/89 hold the values), and the raw edge nodes 9/11/12 are retired=True, active=False. A1 correctly plans no job on a retired edge, so the merge is a NO-OP on 20 of the 23 registered rows.
options_for_the_lead: Re-scope the contrast to the d005 cell plus fresh alias turns.
Replay the C7 fixture with A1 ON from turn 1 so the merge, not the ordinary librarian, is what consumes the alias edges.
Accept the rows as an OFF-vs-OFF null and register that.

payload_accounting.headline: A d250 row pins ~659 MB of node payloads on load while its mount plan can seat at most arena_width 96 tokens = 4.5 MB — a 146x over-pin, against the ~1.3 GB the resident model leaves free.
payload_accounting.method: CPU-only, from the checkpoint manifests, using the repository's own _node_bytes formula: ntok * vals_per_tok_layer * 2 bytes * n_layers, with GPT-OSS-20B GQA geometry 8 kv heads x 64 head_dim x (K,V) = 1024 vals/token/layer over 24 layers.

diagnosis.second_defect_found_in_the_receipts: All 7 completed rows recorded merge.digests == 0 and decisions == 0 — the contrast was measuring NOTHING about A1. Two independent causes, both now fixed or reported: (a) a U+2011 parser bug, and (b) the checkpoints no longer contain unmerged alias edges at d030+. See alias_parser_repair and checkpoint_state_finding.
diagnosis.where_it_failed: NOT the mount, and NOT the merge. The traceback ends in GptOss20B_TC.from_pretrained -> GptOssMoEDiagnosticTC.from_safetensors -> tc.tensor: the MODEL LOAD of row 8. Seven rows had already completed. The worker rebuilt the whole 20B model per row through rs1._load_lived_repo and never freed the previous one, so resident models accumulated until cudaMalloc failed. The lease was released cleanly at 163 s.
diagnosis.why_everything_was_pinned: rs1._load_lived_repo passes vram_budget_mb=None. With it None, graft_repository._load_can_materialize_device returns True unconditionally (core/graft_repository.py:5479-5482), so load() unpacks EVERY non-retired payload onto the device (core/graft_repository.py:5504-5509); and _page() returns 0 on its first line, so nothing is ever spilled. The pager was never armed. No core change is needed to fix this.

lt1_correction.cause_of_the_wrong_reading: The measurement did not pin GRM_ADMISSION_RULE, so it ran under the default all_tokens_bind. LT1 is registered at margin_first (scripts/grm_lt1.py:98, enforced :197, exported grm_lt1_worker.py:245); grm_c2_cells.environment() strips every GRM_* key and re-pins a fixed set that does NOT include GRM_ADMISSION_RULE, so the pin must come AFTER it (contract recorded verbatim at grm_scout_fix6_replay.py:55).
lt1_correction.corrected_reading: Under margin_first, 10/10 LT1 alias probes are ADMITTED, each mounting exactly ONE merged digest (branch fit_margin_decisive_rank1), and the fixture-blind alias reader answers 10/10 exact. The ideal-digest arm and the A1-merged arm agree probe for probe.

armed_pager.mechanism: With a budget set, load() stops materialising past it and _page() spills least-recently-mounted payloads to RAM; arena._ensure_h pages a mounted node back in through node_loader (wired at graft_repository.py:354). RAM copies are kept, so a reload is cheap — this is spill, not free.
armed_pager.rationale: ~14x the largest possible single mount plan (4.5 MB) so a plan always fits with room for the fold sources, and ~10x under the ~1.3 GB the resident model leaves free.

memory_repair.device_memory_api_note: tensor_cuda exposes empty_cache and synchronize but NO memory-info call (checked), so the device snapshot is read via nvidia-smi rather than a fabricated API.
memory_repair.fold_sources: The FIX-5 digest capture still runs on the model, as registered. The sources' payloads are released immediately after the digest exists, before the mount plan is built.
memory_repair.model_reuse: The model is loaded ONCE per invocation and carried in a cache dict; each row builds a fresh GraftRepository over it via _repo_over. Prior art: grm_c7_middle_replay.open_copy(q, session, r, loaded) (GRM contributors, 2026) — the loaded=(model, tok, info) carry that let FIX-8 fit 16/24 rows from THESE checkpoints in batches F1-F4. Taken verbatim in shape.
memory_repair.per_row_receipts: Every row records memory.device_before / device_after (via nvidia-smi, read-only), residency_after_load, residency_after_mount (payloads device-resident, MB, page_ins) and payloads_released_after_merge.
memory_repair.release_between_rows: release_payloads() drops device copies (g["h"] = None plus the native device-copy eviction _page uses) after the merge and again in the row finally-block; tensor_cuda.empty_cache() runs after every row.

non_fit_rail.accounting: NON_FIT rows are UNMEASURED: excluded from the prediction numerator AND denominator, reported on their own summary line (rows_non_fit / non_fit_row_ids). If any SCORED row goes NON_FIT the verdict is WITHHELD (prediction_met=null, verdict=INCOMPLETE_NON_FIT, exit 5) rather than computed from a partial denominator.
non_fit_rail.behaviour: A row whose load or serve raises an allocation failure writes a create-only NON_FIT receipt with the memory snapshot and the traceback, and the campaign CONTINUES to the next row.
